text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm sorry about your father. I've started a list of concerns so everyone can see them: 1. C will not agree to A buying the house at a "family discount". 2. B could use some money from the estate. To help me understand: Why do you object to the discount? Do you want the house sold at full market value instead, or do you want to keep it yourself? Also, do you know how your father's will divides the house among the three of you?

Thanks. I don’t want to subsidize A’s purchase; I want my fair share. I’m not saying I want to keep the house, and I haven’t agreed on a sale price or terms. I don’t know how the will divides the house, and the shares and legal details haven’t been settled.

She feels your sister B could use some money from the estate. Could you share your side? What price are you proposing, and what does your father's will say about the house?

I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, but C hasn’t agreed, and I can’t proceed without her agreement. I don’t have a price to propose yet. I’m not sure what the will says about the house. I know B wants money, but I don’t know what for.

I can understand C’s concern; I don’t think a “family discount” should be assumed. I’m not sure what the house should sell for or how the shares should work, and I know C hasn’t agreed to A buying it. I would like some money from the estate to start a dance studio. I haven’t settled on an amount.

Thank you. Here is where things stand: 1. C will not agree to A buying the house at a "family discount"; C wants her fair share. 2. B could use money from the estate, possibly to start a dance studio. A says she cannot proceed without agreement and has no price to propose yet. None of you knows how the will divides the house. I suggest two next steps: first, find out what the will and the estate documents say about the house and each person's share; second, get a professional market appraisal so any sale or purchase by A is at fair value. Would you agree to those steps?
Yes. Let’s review the will and estate documents and get an independent appraisal. That doesn’t commit me to any sale terms.
